 A Soulé never seen before: key goals and assists, the new Matias has taken Roma by storm
 Serie A 
 Calcio 
 The Argentine has won over Gasp with starring displays and rising numbers: now he is also targeting the Seleccion
 Alessio D'Urso 
 30 october (updated at 09:18) - MILANO 
 English 
 Italiano 
 Deutsch 
 Choose Gazzetta as your preferred source on Google 
 He has chosen the path of the greats: no hesitation, just heavy goals and precious assists. With that low centre of gravity, the ball glued to his left foot and his gaze already cast beyond the defensive line, the "new" Matias Soulé has taken Roma by storm with a start to the season that hints at definitive maturity. It is not just the numbers that impress, but above all the electricity Matias sparks every time he touches the ball: an unpredictability that shifts momentum and upends the plans of opposing defenders, giving the Giallorossi's play the verticality required by Gian Piero Gasperini's attacking brand of football.
 VIDEO: Gasperini risponde ad Allegri: "Ci sono i numeri. Constatazione infelice" 
 Flying start
—   Thus Matias, coinciding also with Paulo Dybala's absence through injury, took Roma by the hand, demonstrating with facts a significant growth that surprised Gasp himself. Following a summer spent on a knife-edge between doubts and rumours of a departure to balance the books, the Argentine has racked up 770 minutes across the league and Champions League with 3 goals and 3 assists. Better even than last season, when he scored 3 goals and provided 2 key passes, with form reminiscent of his first year at Frosinone, the one that revealed the ex-Juve talent. It is a step up in quality from which the team is benefiting in terms of attacking threat and a psychological boost during difficult moments, as demonstrated—for instance—by the crucial goals against Atalanta in the 96th minute (the 2-1 winner) and against Napoli, the goal that sparked the Giallorossi comeback at the Maradona.
 At the end of the tunnel
—   That Argentine lad not even 20 years old who amazed Serie A with Frosinone and scored 5 goals with 1 assist in 767 minutes in the opening nine matchdays, three years on has taken centre stage through the strength of his talent, fully justifying the €30m Roma spent to sign him from Juve. To be sure, not all starts were easy and positive, as seen in his first year in Giallorossi colours under De Rossi and Juric, but from the following season the tune changed after nine matchdays: 3 goals and 2 assists in 666 minutes, and often the decisive man even when Roma were not playing their best football (the goals against Pisa and Verona...). Then, unfortunately, pubalgia complicated the season significantly and, towards the end, Soulé failed to establish himself, even ending up on the list of potential departures. Yet, at his moment of greatest difficulty, the Argentine dug deep, training through the summer to be ready for Gasp. And so, at the end of the tunnel, Mati saw a bright light once again, causing a sensation at the Olimpico, facing teams like Real Madrid without fear and boosting numbers that speak for themselves: an average of 2.78 shots on target per match and 2.22 successful dribbles.
 Sacrifice
—   And to his attacking statistics, Soulé has also managed to add two-way work, drive and pressing on the ball-carriers, which Gasperini demands to guarantee team balance. Now that he sees the season in a different light, Mati can also claim a place for Argentina (where he made his debut on 4 October against Burkina Faso in Messi's farewell matches for the national team) and await the return of his friend Dybala to star alongside him in more matches. The real Soulé has chosen the path of the top players, truly, turning expectations into full-blown establishment in nine matchdays.
